description: Infrastructure-as-code rules: Terraform, Kubernetes, Docker Compose, CloudFormation.

rules.title: Security group ingress open to the internet
rules.remediation: Restrict the CIDR to the networks that need access. If it must be public, confirm the port belongs on the internet - 0.0.0.0/0 on 22, 3389, 5432, 3306, 6379, 9200, or 27017 is how databases end up in breach reports.

rules.title: Administrative port exposed to the internet
rules.remediation: Put the service behind a bastion, VPN, or private subnet. Database and remote-admin ports should never accept connections from the whole internet.

rules.title: Object storage ACL allows public access
rules.remediation: Public buckets are enumerated constantly by automated scanners. Use a CloudFront/CDN origin-access identity for public assets and keep the bucket private.

rules.title: S3 public-access block disabled
rules.remediation: Leave all four public-access-block settings enabled unless the bucket is deliberately a public website, and even then prefer a CDN.

rules.title: Managed database marked publicly accessible
rules.remediation: Place the instance in a private subnet and reach it through the application tier or a bastion.

rules.title: Encryption at rest disabled
rules.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. It is free or near-free on every major provider and is usually a compliance requirement.

rules.title: IAM policy grants wildcard action on wildcard resource
rules.remediation: Action:* on Resource:* is administrator access. Enumerate the specific API calls the workload makes and scope resources by ARN.

rules.title: EC2 instance metadata v1 still permitted
rules.remediation: Set http_tokens = "required" to enforce IMDSv2. IMDSv1 is what turns a simple SSRF into stolen instance credentials.

rules.title: Audit logging or versioning disabled
rules.remediation: Without versioning and access logs you cannot investigate or recover from an incident. Enable both.

rules.title: Privileged container
rules.remediation: A privileged container has effectively root on the host: all capabilities, device access, and a straightforward path to node takeover. Drop it and add only the specific capabilities needed.

rules.title: Container shares a host namespace
rules.remediation: Sharing the host network or PID namespace removes the isolation boundary - the container can see and signal host processes and bind host ports.

rules.title: Container configured to run as root
rules.remediation: Set runAsNonRoot: true and a numeric non-zero runAsUser. Running as root inside a container makes any escape immediately more valuable.

rules.title: Privilege escalation permitted in container
rules.remediation: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false so setuid binaries inside the container cannot gain capabilities.

rules.title: Dangerous Linux capability added to container
rules.remediation: SYS_ADMIN is close to full root; SYS_MODULE loads kernel modules; SYS_PTRACE reads other processes' memory. Drop ALL and add back only what is required.

rules.title: Docker socket or host root mounted into a container
rules.remediation: Mounting the Docker socket grants control of every container on the node, which is a container escape by design. Mounting host /, /etc, or /proc is equivalent. Use a purpose-built API instead.

rules.title: RBAC rule grants wildcard verbs or resources
rules.remediation: Wildcard verbs on wildcard resources is cluster-admin. Enumerate the specific verbs and resources the service account needs.

rules.title: Binding to the cluster-admin role
rules.remediation: Confirm the subject genuinely needs full cluster control. A compromised workload with this binding owns the cluster.

rules.title: Secret value set as a literal environment variable
rules.remediation: Reference a Secret with valueFrom.secretKeyRef instead of a literal value. Literal env values are visible to anyone with pod read access and are stored in the manifest history.

rules.title: Docker Compose port published on all interfaces
rules.remediation: Bind to 127.0.0.1 for services that only need to be reachable from the host: "127.0.0.1:5432:5432".
